rules.title: npm installs are slow and repeated

estimate.assumption: pnpm or bun warm-cache installs are commonly 2-10x faster than cold npm; 0.5 is conservative

rules.why: npm re-extracts every package into node_modules on each run.
rules.fix: Switch to pnpm or bun, or at least add --prefer-offline --no-audit --no-fund.

rules.title: webpack builds dominate time

estimate.assumption: rspack is a near drop-in and typically 3-10x faster; vite for new apps; 0.5 is conservative

rules.why: webpack is single-threaded JS; Rust bundlers parallelise and cache better.
rules.fix: Try rspack (drop-in config) or vite; verify plugin compatibility first.

rules.title: jest runs are a large share of time

estimate.assumption: vitest reuses the Vite transform pipeline and is commonly 2-5x faster on large suites

rules.why: jest transforms every file through Babel/ts-jest and starts a heavy worker per file.
rules.fix: Migrate to vitest (API-compatible for most suites), or at least use --onlyChanged / --changedSince and swc transform.

rules.title: eslint/prettier run slowly and often

estimate.assumption: biome/oxlint are 10-50x faster on raw lint; --cache gives a smaller gain; 0.6 assumes partial rule parity

rules.why: Uncached eslint re-lints the whole tree on each call.
rules.fix: Add --cache, lint only changed files, or move to biome/oxlint where rules allow.
rules.after: eslint --cache <changed files>   # or: biome check --changed, once biome is a dev dependency

rules.title: tsc run from scratch repeatedly

estimate.assumption: incremental type checking typically drops repeat runs by 3-6x; tsgo (native port) is faster again

rules.why: Without incremental, every call re-checks the whole project.
rules.fix: Enable "incremental": true (tsBuildInfoFile) or use --incremental; consider tsgo.
rules.after: npx tsc --noEmit --incremental   # or: tsgo --noEmit, once it is a dev dependency
